Subject: Clarify committed units and SLA credits — draft SOW v3

Hi Laura,

Thanks for sending over SOW v3. Procurement had a few open items before we can route to legal: primarily the definition of the committed units and how throughput maps to our load profile, and the SLA credit calculation when throughput degrades.

Questions we flagged:
- The term "Capacity Unit" in Section 2: is that per-GPU-hour, or per-concurrent-session baseline?
- We run many short-chat calls (average 85 tokens/request, 250 calls/sec during peak). How does Redwood map a committed pool to our qps profile?
- SLA credits: the draft ties credits to "availability" measured at pool-level. We need an explicit formula showing how credits scale with sustained throughput shortfall over rolling 24h windows.

I attached the SOW for reference. Can you share suggested redline language for definitions and a proposed remedy ladder we can circulate with legal?

Best,
Elena
Director, Cloud Engineering
Fontaine Health

Hi Elena — thanks, and great questions. I've sketched proposed redline language below and attached our internal glossary doc that maps pool sizing to common workload profiles. High level:

1) Capacity Unit definition (proposed):
   - "Committed Capacity Unit (CCU): one CCU equals one (1) effective GPU-hour of inference capacity measured at 16k context throughput for baseline models. The CCU is a billing and entitlement unit and is independent of model choice; conversion factors apply per model as listed in Appendix A."

2) Throughput mapping:
   - We recommend sizing using a throughput conversion table rather than raw qps. For short-chat (your 85 token average) we map token-rate and med-latency targets to an effective CCU consumption per 1,000 requests. See attached table in Redwood-Terms-Dedicated-Defns.docx.

3) SLA / Remedy ladder (summary):
   - Remedy triggers use a "Sustained Throughput Shortfall" metric: if realized pool token throughput < 90% of committed throughput for a rolling 24h window, customer is eligible for credits on a sliding scale (5%-40% of monthly commit pro rata depending on severity and duration). Full detail in proposed clause.

I've attached a draft redline file (Redwood-Terms-Dedicated-Defns.docx) with exact clause language. Two asks for you: 1) confirm your peak calculation (250 calls/sec × 85 tokens avg = X tokens/sec) and whether you prefer the CCU anchored at 16k context or 8k; 2) any procurement thresholds for credits (e.g., maximum cumulative credits per year).

If helpful, Marcus can run a quick sizing calc to translate your traffic into CCUs and a sample credit impact.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Laura / Elena — quick sizing note from infra:

Elena, using the numbers you provided (250 calls/sec × 85 tokens = 21,250 tokens/sec peak). Assuming 95% cache efficiency on prefix reuse and batching targeting 16ms p50 per token on our T4-equivalent pool, the conservative mapping is: ~45 CCUs for steady-state peak; burst buffer and headroom add another 15 CCUs. So recommended committed pool = 60 CCUs.

On CCU definition: anchoring at 16k context gives more headroom for models with longer histories; however if Fontaine's workloads are strictly short-chat we can rebase CCU to 8k for lower nominal consumption (we'd then apply conversion factors per model).

SLA credit formula suggestion (concrete):
- Define shortfall S = max(0, (CommittedThroughput - ObservedThroughput)/CommittedThroughput) measured over rolling 24h.
- If S > 0.10 for >= 6 consecutive hours in the 24h window, credit = MIN(MonthlyCommitFee × (0.05 + 0.35 × (S - 0.10)/0.90), MonthlyCommitFee × 0.40).
- Annual cap: credits may not exceed 50% of annual committed spend without executive approval.

I'll also include a sample amortization table showing credits at different S values so procurement has a clear delta.

-Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Laura / Marcus — thanks for the speedy turn. Circling back after internal review with procurement and SRE:

1) The CCU anchored at 8k context makes more sense for our current usage pattern. If conversion factors are documented clearly in Appendix A we can accept that approach; please mark the change in the redline.

2) Sizing: the 60 CCU recommendation is in the ballpark we expected. Procurement asked whether there is a stepped discount if we commit 12 months vs 36 months — i.e., can you provide the commit pricing tiers you mentioned on the sales call and how that affects the monthly commit fee used in the credit calculation?

3) SLA credits: procurement wants the formula simplified to be easier to audit. Their request: replace the piecewise formula with a linear credit = MonthlyCommitFee × min(0.40, 0.80 × S) with an explicit minimum trigger S >= 0.15 for any credit. They will accept the annual cap at 50% but want a quarterly reporting clause and the ability to run an independent audit if cumulative credits exceed 25% of quarterly spend.

We can likely accept the redline once the CCU anchor, the commit-tier pricing schedule, and the simplified credit formula are reflected. Can you provide an updated redline with those three changes and a sample 12/24/36-month price table?

If we get that by Friday 5/28, procurement will circulate to legal the same day.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Cloud Engineering
Fontaine Health
